evidence_basis.originality_note: All seven contexts, wording, values and planned diagrams are original. The mapped official evidence informed only the derivation, explanation and multi-step demand patterns.

question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Question 1 directly retrieves pressure from Lesson 7. Question 7 combines that pressure-force relationship with the current hydrostatic pressure-difference model.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: direct retrieval, three diagnostic concept choices, guided column derivation, general two-depth derivation, then a mixed pressure-force application

questions.prompt: State the definition of pressure and rearrange its equation to make normal force F the subject.
A vertical column of liquid has density ρ, cross-sectional area A and height h. Which expression gives the mass of the column?
In a derivation for a straight liquid column, its weight is ρAhg and the pressure increase at its base is found from weight divided by base area. Why does the final expression contain no A?

options.A: The liquid has no weight when it is static.
options.B: A is always equal to one square metre.
options.C: Both the column weight and the area over which it acts increase in the same proportion.
options.D: Pressure is found by multiplying force by area.

questions.prompt: Points R and S are in the same static liquid. S is 0.40 m vertically below R. A pipe joining them follows a curved route of length 1.2 m. Which distance belongs in the hydrostatic pressure-difference relationship?

options.A: 0.40 m, because only vertical depth difference is relevant
options.B: 1.2 m, because pressure follows the full pipe route
options.C: 0.80 m, because the two distances must be subtracted
options.D: 1.6 m, because the two distances must be added

questions.prompt: A straight-sided vessel contains a static liquid of density ρ to depth h. Its horizontal base has area A. Starting from the controlled definitions of density and pressure, derive the pressure difference between the liquid surface and the base. State one assumption used.

figure.purpose: Assess construction of the complete column derivation from labelled geometry
figure.brief: Original black-and-white straight-sided vessel containing liquid. Label only density rho, vertical depth h and base area A. Include no volume, mass, weight, force arrows, formula or solution steps.
figure.alt_text: A straight liquid column has density rho, depth h and base area A.

questions.prompt: An imaginary vertical slab of static liquid has horizontal area A and lies between two levels separated vertically by Δh. The pressure is p₁ at the upper level and p₂ at the lower level. Draw or state the three vertical forces on the slab, use equilibrium to derive an expression for p₂ - p₁, and explain why the result would be unchanged if a different value of A were chosen.

figure.purpose: Assess an original two-depth force-balance derivation without revealing force directions
figure.brief: Original black-and-white rectangular imaginary liquid slab between two dotted horizontal levels. Label upper pressure p1, lower pressure p2, horizontal area A and vertical separation delta-h. Leave clear space for learner force arrows. Do not include force arrows, weight, equations or answers.
figure.alt_text: An imaginary liquid slab lies between pressures p1 and p2 at levels separated by delta h.

questions.prompt: Two faces of a flexible circular diaphragm are connected to two points in the same static oil. The second point is 0.75 m vertically below the first. The oil density is 860 kg m⁻³, g is 9.81 N kg⁻¹ and the diaphragm area is 2.40 × 10⁻³ m². Derive the pressure difference from a force balance on an imaginary liquid slab, calculate its value, then use the previous lesson's pressure relationship to calculate the resultant normal force on the diaphragm. State the direction of this force relative to the higher-pressure side.
